page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.12xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It runs an Intel Xeon 8488C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz, providing 48 burstable vCPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU incorporates 105 MB of L3 cache alongside specialized instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity is configured at 96.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not feature local storage disks, requiring remote EBS volumes, and has no discrete GPU accelerators. Networking baseline throughput is rated at 9 Gbps.

Benchmark results show competitive throughput across multi-threaded and vector computing tasks. The c7i-flex.12xlarge achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 19030.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 65056.32, landing in the top quartile of tested instances. Hardware instruction extensions such as AMX and AVX-512 enable strong performance in CPU-based artificial intelligence tasks; the instance delivers 353.0 tokens per second on small 135M parameter LLM text generation (top 10%) and 30.87 tokens per second on 7B parameter models. Memory throughput is also strong, registering 222.1 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB block reads and supporting 62.18 million Redis SET operations per second.

Because the Flex tier utilizes a burstable CPU allocation model, it delivers compute-focused resources at a lower qualitative cost profile than fixed-capacity instances, provided continuous peak utilization is not sustained. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage and reliance on a 9 Gbps baseline network mean network-bound or disk-intensive IOPS tasks depend heavily on separate EBS volumes. The instance is suitable for compute-heavy workloads that experience variable demand, such as software compilation, batch processing, static web serving clusters, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with burstable CPU allocation, it provides 48 vCPUs (24 physical cores) and 96.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute memory ratio. It does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, relying on remote EBS volumes and a 9 Gbps baseline network. Supported by AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions, the instance demonstrates high benchmark scores in Clang software compilation, Redis key-value operations (62.18 million SET operations per second), and CPU-based lightweight LLM inference. The flex allocation offers a cost-effective alternative for variable CPU demand, making it suitable for distributed web serving, CI/CD pipelines, and batch compute workloads.
